clue.text: Splendid adage for one not working against the grain

definitions.text: one not working against the grain

parts.note: ripping is old British slang for splendid or excellent
a saw is an old saying or proverb

explanation.surface: Someone praises a fine old proverb about a person who never goes against the grain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'against the grain' sounds like a figure of speech about nonconformists, but a carpenter's saw that cuts along the grain is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: This saw is the tool designed to cut wood along the grain rather than across it.

clue.text: Stop and turn away

definitions.meaning: to cease or halt suddenly, as in a conversation
to detach yourself or end a relationship

explanation.surface: An instruction to halt and look elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to halt abruptly and to separate or withdraw from something.

clue.text: Region sadly showing neglect

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters of region are put in disorder

explanation.surface: A whole area is visibly left uncared-for.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay no attention to something is to neglect it, a straightforward verb synonym.

clue.text: Cross-channel dash

parts.note: a dash means flair or verve, and this word for it is borrowed from across the English Channel, from French

explanation.surface: A quick dash over the Channel to France.
explanation.definitionFit: This French borrowing means vigour, style and dash, so it is the dash from across the Channel.

clue.text: He minds his own business

parts.note: read literally, a person who looks after a business that belongs to him, not a discreet person

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps out of other people's affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: An owner who runs a shop or firm literally minds a business that is his own.

clue.text: Came with servants?

parts.note: both turned up at an event, and was waited on by servants

explanation.surface: A grand guest arriving with a retinue.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both was present at something and was waited upon by attendants.

clue.text: Blood group

definitions.meaning: blood means kin, relatives by birth, as in 'blood is thicker than water'

explanation.surface: A medical blood group classification.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means one's kin by blood and also any related grouping, such as a family of plants.

clue.text: Pass lightly over a point on a Kipling character

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written on top of another comes first

parts.note: S, south, is a point of the compass
Kim is the boy hero of Rudyard Kipling's novel of that name

explanation.surface: Glancing quickly over a remark about a figure from Kipling.
explanation.definitionFit: To skim is to glide over a surface or read something quickly and superficially.

clue.text: Not even a soldier

definitions.meaning: uneven, not regular in shape or pattern
a soldier not in the regular army, such as a guerrilla

explanation.surface: A remark that not even one soldier came.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means uneven or unsymmetrical, and as a noun a member of an unofficial fighting force.

clue.text: Used by athletes, it helps to make a record

definitions.meaning: the running circuit athletes race on

definitions.text: it helps to make a record
definitions.meaning: a single song or piece on an album

explanation.surface: Something athletes use that helps them set a record.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a world record on the running circuit; the second sense is a recording, made up of several songs.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an athletics running circuit and one song among several on a vinyl album.

clue.text: Part company with philosopher — there's no comeback

parts.note: Plato was the ancient Greek philosopher

indicators.note: a comeback is a return, so the word no is read in the opposite direction

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a group with a great thinker and never returns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part company' looks like a verb meaning separate; read it as a noun phrase, a part of a company of soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: This military unit is a subdivision of an infantry company, so it is literally part of a company.

clue.text: Cover charge?

parts.note: not a restaurant's fee per diner but the price paid for insurance cover

explanation.surface: The extra fee a restaurant adds for each place laid.
explanation.definitionFit: Policyholders pay this regular sum to an insurer in return for cover.

clue.text: Loop line quickly turns east

indicators.note: turns says the word for quickly is read back to front

parts.note: soon means before long, in a short time

explanation.surface: A railway loop line rapidly bends towards the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loop line' suggests a railway branch; it is a rope or line tied in a loop.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangman's or lasso's knot is a loop made in a length of rope or line.

clue.text: Revolutionary device saves people from pegging out

definitions.text: Revolutionary device saves people from pegging out

parts.words: Revolutionary device saves people from pegging out
parts.note: a machine that whirls round and so spares people from hanging washing on a line with pegs, not one that saves lives

explanation.surface: A radical invention keeps people from dying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pegging out' is British slang for dying, but also means hanging laundry on a line with clothes-pegs; 'revolutionary' means spinning.
explanation.definitionFit: This household appliance spins wet clothes fast to remove water, so they need not be pegged on a line.

clue.text: Rocking and rolling

definitions.meaning: astonishing, shocking, as in news that rocks you
lurching or swaying unsteadily on one's feet

explanation.surface: A description of rock and roll music.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both astounding, as news that rocks you, and tottering or reeling while walking.

clue.text: Limited form of credit after period of unemployment

indicators.note: after places the shuffled letters following the word for a break from work

parts.note: a rest is a time spent not working

indicators.note: form of suggests the letters of credit are given a new shape

explanation.surface: Only a restricted type of credit is available once someone has been out of work.
explanation.definitionFit: Something restricted is kept within limits, a direct adjective synonym.

clue.text: Sheds tears often enough to demonstrate compassion

indicators.note: the letters of the three words are rearranged so as to show a new word, the demonstration

explanation.surface: Someone who often cries is plainly compassionate.
explanation.definitionFit: Being tender-hearted and kindly is having compassion, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Having caught the eye, got married

definitions.meaning: caught by a hook as a fish is, or captivated by something
informal for joined up as a couple, wed

explanation.surface: Someone noticed and promptly wed.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means caught on a hook, so captivated, and also, informally, joined in marriage.

clue.text: Key leather treatment is delicate

parts.note: E is a musical key

indicators.note: a treatment works the material over, so the letters of leather are rearranged

explanation.surface: A process applied to important leather makes it fine.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethereal means extremely light and delicate, almost too fine for this world.

clue.text: Scrap merchant?

parts.note: scrap is slang for a fight, so this is someone who deals in fights rather than scrap metal

explanation.surface: A dealer in scrap metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who stirs up and promotes fighting between nations trades, figuratively, in scraps.

clue.text: Where, abroad, you'll see us in a form of sari

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the reshaped letters
a form of means the letters of sari are reshaped

explanation.surface: Somewhere overseas we appear in a variant of the Indian garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Russia is a foreign country, so a place abroad, as the question where expects.

clue.text: The gold edging makes this different

indicators.note: edging means the word for gold borders the article's letters on both sides

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A gold trim sets something apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Other means different or distinct from the one already mentioned.

clue.text: Pompous point to hold forth about

indicators.note: about means the speech word goes round the other letter

parts.note: orate means to speak at length, pompously
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: An instruction to lecture someone self-important.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornate means elaborately decorated, which of a speech or style is pompous and showy.

clue.text: French chemist late on his way back

parts.note: past means late, former, as in past glories

indicators.note: back means the word for street is read in reverse

parts.note: rue is the French for street, so the way of a Frenchman

explanation.surface: A French scientist running late returns home.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Pasteur was the French chemist who developed pasteurisation and vaccines.

clue.text: Like things to eat

parts.note: food items famously alike, as in the saying 'like two of these in a pod'

explanation.surface: Someone states their favourite foods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like' is not the verb of enjoying but the adjective 'alike'.
explanation.definitionFit: These green vegetables are a byword for things identical to each other, from the phrase about a pod.

clue.text: Information going to one boy is applicable to the whole class

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
Eric is one boy's name

explanation.surface: News going to a single lad is relevant to the whole class.
explanation.definitionFit: Generic means relating to a whole group or class rather than to an individual.

clue.text: Nuts: crack almonds to start with

parts.note: a crack is a joke or wisecrack, a gag

indicators.note: to start with picks the first letter of almonds

explanation.surface: Instructions for cracking almonds first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' and 'almonds' set a kitchen scene, but 'Nuts' means mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal for crazy or out of one's mind.

clue.text: Farewell notice that's going to university

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, a public notice
i.e. stands for id est, 'that is'

explanation.surface: A goodbye message from someone heading off to university.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a French-derived word for goodbye, used in English as a farewell.

clue.text: Dark horse at 20 to 1 causing an upset?

parts.note: night is the dark part of the day
a mare is a female horse

explanation.surface: An outsider at long odds wins a race and shocks everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: A 20-1 outsider winning is a bookmaker's disaster, so the definition is the whole scenario described.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-odds winner is a dreadful ordeal for the betting firms, a bad dream that costs them money.
